source.publisher: U.S. Dept. of State, OFAC (U.S. Dept. of the Treasury), U.S. Coast Guard
source.title: Guidance to Address Illicit Shipping and Sanctions Evasion Practices (Sanctions Advisory for the Maritime Industry, Energy and Metals Sectors)

summary: This joint advisory from the U.S. Department of State, OFAC, and the U.S. Coast Guard (May 14, 2020) updates prior sanctions-related shipping advisories concerning Iran, North Korea, and Syria. It describes deceptive shipping practices used to evade sanctions: AIS disabling/manipulation ('spoofing'), physically altering vessel identification, falsifying cargo and vessel documents, ship-to-ship (STS) transfers, voyage irregularities including indirect routing and transshipment through third countries, false flags and flag hopping, and complex ownership or management structures using shell companies to disguise beneficial ownership. Annex A gives sector-specific due diligence guidance for insurers, flag registries, port authorities, industry associations, commodity traders, financial institutions, ship owners/operators/charterers, classification societies, vessel captains, and crewing companies. Annex B details North Korea-, Iran-, and Syria-specific sanctions authorities and documented deceptive practices, including North Korean coal and sand exports via STS transfers to Chinese barges, illicit refined-petroleum imports via STS transfers, non-AIS-transmitting barges, and Iranian oil-for-Syria schemes that benefited the IRGC-Qods Force, Hizballah, and Hamas.

citations.quote: vessels engaged in illicit activities may also intentionally disable their AIS transponders or manipulate the data transmitted in order to mask their movement.
Bad actors may falsify the flag of their vessels to mask illicit trade.  They may also repeatedly register with new flag states (“flag hopping”) to avoid detection.
STS transfers—especially at night or in areas determined to be high-risk for sanctions evasion or other illicit activity—are frequently used to evade sanctions
North Korea sometimes utilizes non-ocean-going barges that do not transmit an AIS signal to illicitly transport North Korea-origin goods to China.

Bad actors attempt to take advantage of this complexity through the use of complex business structures, including those involving shell companies and/or multiple levels of ownership and management, to disguise the ultimate beneficial owner of cargo or commodities

Malign actors may attempt to disguise the ultimate destination or origin of cargo or recipients by using indirect routing, unscheduled detours, or transit or transshipment of cargo through third countries.
The majority of these exports have occurred via STS transfers from North Korea-flagged vessels to local barges in Chinese territorial sea.

Authorities have found that sanctions evaders have falsified shipping documentation pertaining to petrochemicals, petroleum, petroleum products, or metals (steel, iron) or sand in order to disguise their origin.
Recognizing that purchases of crude and refined petroleum, petrochemicals, and metals at rates significantly below market prices may be red flags indicating illicit behavior.

typologies.label: Trade Value Offsetting for Terrorist Proxy Financing

citations.quote: This scheme used a payment offsetting arrangement in which the sale and shipment of Iranian oil to Syria provided hundreds of millions of dollars to Iran's terror proxy groups, including Hizballah, HAMAS, and the IRGC-QF.

typologies.review_justification: Found in Syria section, deceptive shipping practices case study, page 35. No KC typology names this mechanism; search for 'trade proceeds used to finance terrorism proxy militant groups' returned no match above floor. SAN006 Trade Based Sanctions Evasion requires 'mispricing an invoice, or misdescribing the goods' -- absent here; this is a settlement mechanism (offsetting, not cash) routing value to a terrorist beneficiary. SAN002/SAN003 concern vessel-identity/routing concealment, not financing routing. TBML006 Circular Trade requires 'value leaves an entity and returns to it' (closed loop) -- here value moves forward Iran->Syria->Hizballah/HAMAS/IRGC-QF with no round-trip. This is a distinct trade-settlement-as-terrorist-financing-conduit mechanism the library does not capture.

citations.quote: Malign actors constantly seek novel ways to exploit global supply chains for their benefit.

indicators.description: Vessels intentionally disable AIS transponders or manipulate transmitted data ('spoofing') to broadcast a different name, IMO number, MMSI or other identifying information, masking movement.

citations.quote: The practice of manipulating AIS data, referred to as “spoofing,” allows ships to broadcast a different name, International Maritime Organization (IMO) number (a unique, seven-digit vessel identification code), Maritime Mobile Service Identity (MMSI), or other identifying information.

indicators.description: Vessels painted over names and IMO numbers on hull/superstructure to obscure identity and pass as different vessels.

citations.quote: Vessels involved in illicit activities have often painted over vessel names and IMO numbers to obscure their identities and pass themselves off as different vessels.

indicators.description: Falsified shipping documentation (bills of lading, certificates of origin, invoices) for petrochemicals, petroleum, metals or sand used to disguise true cargo origin.

citations.quote: Authorities have found that sanctions evaders have falsified shipping documentation pertaining to petrochemicals, petroleum, petroleum products, or metals (steel, iron) or sand in order to disguise their origin.

indicators.description: Ship-to-ship cargo transfers at sea, especially at night or in high-risk areas, used to conceal the origin or destination of petroleum, coal and other material.

citations.quote: STS transfers—especially at night or in areas determined to be high-risk for sanctions evasion or other illicit activity—are frequently used to evade sanctions by concealing the origin or destination of surreptitiously transferred petroleum, coal, and other material.

indicators.description: Indirect routing, unscheduled detours, or transit/transshipment of cargo through third countries used to disguise ultimate cargo origin or destination.

citations.quote: Malign actors may attempt to disguise the ultimate destination or origin of cargo or recipients by using indirect routing, unscheduled detours, or transit or transshipment of cargo through third countries.

indicators.description: Falsification of a vessel's flag and repeated re-registration with new flag states ('flag hopping') to avoid detection, including continued use of a flag after deregistration.

citations.quote: Bad actors may falsify the flag of their vessels to mask illicit trade.  They may also repeatedly register with new flag states (“flag hopping”) to avoid detection.

indicators.description: Use of complex business structures, shell companies and multiple layers of ownership/management to disguise the ultimate beneficial owner of cargo or commodities.

citations.quote: Bad actors attempt to take advantage of this complexity through the use of complex business structures, including those involving shell companies and/or multiple levels of ownership and management, to disguise the ultimate beneficial owner of cargo or commodities

indicators.description: Purchases of crude/refined petroleum, petrochemicals and metals at rates significantly below market price.

citations.quote: Recognizing that purchases of crude and refined petroleum, petrochemicals, and metals at rates significantly below market prices may be red flags indicating illicit behavior.

indicators.description: Use of non-ocean-going barges that do not transmit an AIS signal to illicitly transport North Korea-origin coal and sand to China.

citations.quote: North Korea sometimes utilizes non-ocean-going barges that do not transmit an AIS signal to illicitly transport North Korea-origin goods to China.

indicators.description: Ownership of a vessel transferred between companies controlled by the same beneficial owner with no discernable legitimate purpose for the transfer.

extraction_notes: PAT008 (network family, doctrine authored as NI008) shares the label 'Shadow Fleet' with SAN002 (sanctions family); SAN002 was selected as the closer fit given this document's framing as a sanctions advisory rather than a network-analytics product. TBML004/TBML005/TBML010 were reviewed but not proposed: the document's falsified-documents and underpricing content is narrower and mechanism-specific, so SAN006 (Trade Based Sanctions Evasion) was used at low confidence instead. Russia (RU) and China (CN) are named only as counterparties/destinations in specific case examples (Annex B North Korea coal/sand routes; Syria section jet-fuel sanctions action), not as primary subjects of the advisory. The three unnamed individuals sanctioned alongside Maritime Assistance LLC could not be extracted as the source text does not name them. Merged 1 reviewer addition(s) under schema 1.4.0; each carries its review_justification. Extraction-only record retained at data/records/.
